review.method: Acceptance suite run locally with `retail,gpu,audio` (CS_GAME_DIR, CS_ENGINE_IMAGE): the owner's own command `cs --cs-path $CS_GAME_DIR --mission M01 --smoke-seconds 45 --capture-dir private/evidence/PARITY-M01-ISLAND-SHADING` drove the same windowed composition the owner plays on this machine's GPU — through the launch cinematic, which the smoke watches play out (`launch_cinematic_plays`: 4818 ticks, handed over, 0.000 m drift) before its scripted checks — and wrote the framebuffer PNGs plus report.json, all checks passing (`passed: true`), including `first_control_frame` at the hand-over (the frame the finding compares beside the owner capture `orig25.png`, which is ~25 s into the original flight and never an elapsed-time match). The retail test `accept_parity_m01_island_shading_retail_tile_binds_texture_colour_and_shading` composes M01 through the production path and asserts on the resident island tile `g28614` (mesh slot 781, node-2976): every stored material group reaches a `Mesh3d`+`MeshMaterial3d` child of the world node, each stored texture name resolves to a bound `base_color_texture` (`forest1`, `cliff1`, `sand128` among them), every vertex-coloured part's material is `unlit` with `fog_enabled` kept, and the drawn `Mesh::ATTRIBUTE_COLOR` carries exactly the production render mesh's stored corner colours under the measured `>1 → ×1/255` byte rule — unioned across the normal-split parts. The synthetic members pin `slice_groups` colour preservation and the byte-rule normalization. Mutation checks during development: deleting `stored_shading_materials` and dropping the colour slice each fail the retail test. The run is automated, never `human_play`, and no original executable ran; nothing is `verified_original`. This harness derives every field from the recorded log, production discovery of $CS_GAME_DIR, the smoke's report and the hashes of those artifacts. LIMITS: how the original applied the corner colours is `MaterialUnknown::VertexColorMeaning` (stored brightness does not correlate with stored normals or a sun-direction N·L model), the GameZ materials carry no lighting flags, and the sun-orientation axis semantics stay unknown — recorded in docs/findings/2026-10-19-parity-m01-island-shading.md. Validated with tools/validate_evidence.py (structure and artifact hashes, exit 0); --require-pass reports the recorded unknowns as unresolved issues, which stand as this slice's honest limitations rather than being emptied to pass the gate.
